solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Take note, primarily, of Marx Brothers slinging racial insults in America

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is Latin for 'take note'

indicators.note: primarily means taking the leading letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: The Marx Brothers, in an old film, hurling ugly slurs that an American audience would notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take note' is the Latin nota bene abbreviation, and 'primarily' applies to the four words after the comma, not to 'note'.
explanation.definitionFit: The N-word is a notorious American racial slur, and 'N-bomb' is slang for dropping it, so the plural names such insults.

clue.text: Cable connects peacekeepers with journalist not having to use muscle

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, which sends peacekeeping forces
a flex is an electric cable
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A news cable links the UN peacekeepers with a reporter, with no force needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces sit in answer order: peacekeepers, then cable, then journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscle that is unflexed has not been tensed, so it has not been put to work.

clue.text: Work in quarry, crossing river for soup

parts.note: to mine is to work in, or dig, a pit

indicators.note: the word for quarry spans across the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: stone is what a quarry yields; to stone, or a quarry of stone

explanation.surface: A quarryman crosses a river in search of soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarry' is not the place dug but what it yields; 'crossing' makes the word span the river letter, giving STRONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is the thick Italian vegetable soup, so it is one example of the general word.

clue.text: Shows respect to missile-launchers

definitions.meaning: someone who ... inclines the head or body as a mark of respect

explanation.surface: Respect is paid to the weapons that fire missiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Bending at the waist is a gesture of deference; an archer's weapon propels arrows, so both senses fit the same word.

clue.text: Albanian leader cross — have heron shot!

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: An angry Albanian ruler, in a bad mood, orders a heron shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' scrambles X plus HAVE HERON. Enver Hoxha ruled communist Albania from 1944 until his death in 1985.
explanation.definitionFit: Enver Hoxha was the communist head of state who led Albania for four decades after the Second World War.

clue.text: Actor George starts rehearsing on one foot

indicators.note: starts means the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: A means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: A film actor begins rehearsing a scene while balanced on one foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes R from rehearsing, followed by A and FT.
explanation.definitionFit: George Raft was a Hollywood star of 1930s gangster films such as Scarface, so the surname completes the name.

clue.text: Fruit of Salvadoran geneticists

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is taken from within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A fruit produced by scientists in El Salvador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' points into 'SalvadORAN GEneticists', which holds the answer across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange is a common citrus fruit, so this is an example of the category.

clue.text: Spy's loft conversion puts up bills

indicators.note: a loft conversion rebuilds the space, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A spy's attic, newly converted, is used to put up posters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' rearranges the letters of SPY'S LOFT.
explanation.definitionFit: To flypost is to stick up advertising posters illegally on walls, so it covers fixing up bills.

clue.text: Independent satellite tracking deposit for diplomat

indicators.note: tracking means following behind, so these pieces come after the deposit word

parts.note: to bank money is to deposit it
the Moon is Earth's natural satellite

explanation.surface: An independent satellite follows a bank deposit for a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tracking' means following, so the satellite pieces come after the deposit even though the clue names them first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ban Ki-moon, a South Korean diplomat, served as Secretary-General of the United Nations from 2007 to 2016.

clue.text: March now over with police reserve initially in trouble

indicators.note: in means these initial letters go inside the word for trouble

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the words police and reserve

explanation.surface: Now that March has ended, the police reserve finds itself in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives P and R, and 'in' puts them inside AIL.
explanation.definitionFit: April is the month that comes once March has finished, so it is when March is over.

clue.text: Grey or red hairstyles

definitions.meaning: grey mullet and red mullet are both kinds of fish
a mullet is a haircut short at the front and long at the back

explanation.surface: Choosing between grey or red hair dye for a set of cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grey or red' looks like hair colour but names two species of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey and red are both fish species sharing the name; the haircut, short in front and long behind, has the same name.

clue.text: Consumed drug with peanut mince

parts.note: E is short for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: to mince is to chop finely, so the letters are cut up and reordered

explanation.surface: Someone eats a drug together with minced peanut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' reads as food but is the signal to chop the nut's letters into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eaten up has been completely devoured, so the phrase is a synonym for used up or swallowed.

clue.text: Happens to be back by early evening

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: is means happens to be, exists
X is the sign for 'by', as in 3 x 4 or a room measured 10 by 12

explanation.surface: Someone happens to be home again by early evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like 'home again' but reverses the verb; 'by' is the multiplication sign, a letter-shaped cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Six o'clock is a typical hour at the start of the evening, so the number stands for that time.

clue.text: Campaigners spouting purest rubbish about back-to-front digit

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go around the other piece
rubbish means nonsense, so the letters are scrambled
back-to-front means the final letter is brought round to the start

parts.note: the thumb is a digit of the hand

explanation.surface: Campaigners are spouting utter rubbish about a reversed finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to-front' moves only the digit's last letter to its start (BTHUM); 'rubbish' scrambles the fodder and 'about' wraps it round. 'spouting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tub-thumpers are ranting public speakers who bang the pulpit, so they are vocal campaigners for a cause.

clue.text: Hold famous tea party with hermit?

parts.note: the Boston Tea Party of 1773 was a protest against British tax on tea
a hermit crab is one kind of crab, hence the question mark for a definition by example

explanation.surface: A hermit holds onto a famous tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' is not a verb here but a wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A Boston crab is a wrestling grip in which the attacker bends the opponent's legs back over their body.

clue.text: Unexpectedly dramatic take I see extracted from business intelligence

indicators.note: unexpectedly means the remaining letters turn up in an unforeseen order
extracted from means these letters are pulled out of the larger pool first

parts.note: C sounds like see, a standard crossword letter

explanation.surface: An unexpectedly dramatic take, I see, comes from business intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracted from' removes I and C from DRAMATIC TAKE, and 'Unexpectedly' rearranges the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Market data is commercial information on prices and trading, a form of business intelligence.

clue.text: Medium bill accepted by Ferdinand?

indicators.note: accepted by means the bill word is taken inside the name

parts.note: Rio Ferdinand is a former England footballer, a name given by example
an ad, or advertisement, is a bill

explanation.surface: A medium-sized bill is accepted by a man named Ferdinand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' signals insertion. Ferdinand is a surname: the footballer Rio Ferdinand captained Manchester United and England.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio is a medium of communication, one of the mass media alongside TV and print.

clue.text: Unforthcoming about crime losing its edge seen in colour

parts.note: RE means about, concerning

indicators.note: seen in means the shortened crime goes inside the colour word

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour

indicators.note: losing means those letters drop out of the word crime

parts.note: a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Someone keeps quiet about a crime that was spotted in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its edge' is a synonym to remove, not the outer letters: 'losing' leaves CE, and 'seen in' places that inside the colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticent person is reserved and slow to share their thoughts, a synonym for unforthcoming.

clue.text: A number of Greek characters sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: xi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so xis are Greek characters

explanation.surface: A number of Greek characters are returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses XIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Six is a counting figure, so it is one example of a number.

clue.text: Things to bet on — according to Winstone, did I hear?

indicators.note: did I hear? means the answer sounds like the phrase

parts.note: Ray Winstone is an English actor; what he says is 'Ray says'

explanation.surface: Talk of bets that the actor Winstone apparently recommends.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray Winstone, known for London gangster roles, would say 'Ray says' with a Cockney (East End London) accent, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse or dog races are events on which punters place wagers.

clue.text: In Stuttgart, she loads hydrogen into vehicles for money-handlers

indicators.note: into means the loaded word goes inside the vehicles word

parts.note: cars are vehicles

indicators.note: loads means the German word takes the hydrogen letter on board

parts.note: SIE is German for she, and Stuttgart is a German city
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: In Stuttgart a woman fills hydrogen cars, serving bank clerks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Stuttgart' asks for German, not letters hidden in the city name; 'loads' gives SHIE, and 'into' sends that inside the vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashiers are the bank or shop staff who take and pay out cash, so they handle money.

clue.text: Unlikely hero, yet oddly up a tree greeting solver's arrival

indicators.note: unlikely means the letters fall into an improbable arrangement
oddly means the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: An unlikely hero gets stuck up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlikely' scrambles HERO YET, and 'oddly' takes U, A, R, E from 'up a tree'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is what one says when welcoming someone just turned up, here the solver reaching the answer.

clue.text: Henri Cartier-Bresson starts cycling to expand wealth

indicators.note: cycling means a letter is moved round from the front to the back
starts means the opening letter of the surname

explanation.surface: The photographer Henri Cartier-Bresson takes up cycling to grow his fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' gives C, making HENRIC; 'cycling' moves H to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich is to make richer, increasing riches or worth.

clue.text: Back centre of revolution to expel a number

indicators.note: back means the remaining letters are read in reverse
to expel means the letter A is removed

parts.note: an axis is the line around which something turns

explanation.surface: A central rebel figure, back from a revolution, is expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to expel' takes A from AXIS, and 'Back' reverses XIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Six is an integer, so it is an example of a figure.

clue.text: 90 over 18 for one old British minisub

indicators.note: over in a down entry means the numeral is placed above the next piece

parts.note: XC is 90 in Roman numerals
the answer to 18 across is six, and 6 down's answer is a floating platform

explanation.surface: A wartime submarine of the 1940s, with numbers suggesting age.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 across is SIX, so '18 for one' points to 6 down, RAFT, placed under XC.
explanation.definitionFit: X-craft were small British midget submarines used in the Second World War, such as against the Tirpitz.

clue.text: Pottery figure's from freelancer, am I correct?

indicators.note: figure's from means the answer is to be found from within the following letters

explanation.surface: A freelance potter asks whether a figure's design is right.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'freelanCER AM I Correct'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramic is fired clay ware, so it is an equivalent of earthenware or pots.

clue.text: It inspires birds to keep head down

indicators.note: in a down entry, keeping the head down means the first letter goes to the bottom

parts.note: emus are large flightless birds

explanation.surface: Birds are urged to stay low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep head down' moves E from the front of EMUS to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A muse is a source of creative inspiration, after the nine goddesses of the arts in Greek myth.

clue.text: American friends mostly right to have more offshoots

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is removed

parts.note: buddies is American slang for friends

explanation.surface: American pals are generally right to grow more branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops S from BUDDIES, then R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddier is the comparative of buddy, used here as bearing buds, so it means having more shoots.

clue.text: Scottish bank not very bold

indicators.note: not means the letter for very is taken out

parts.note: brave means bold

explanation.surface: A Scottish bank that is not very daring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes V from BRAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brae is a Scots word for a hillside or steep riverbank.

clue.text: Arrests Stevie?

definitions.meaning: to nick is British slang for arrest
The question mark marks the surname as one example

explanation.surface: Stevie is arrested?
explanation.definitionFit: Nick is British slang for an arrest by police; Stevie Nicks is the Fleetwood Mac singer, so the surname is shared.

clue.text: This taste is discriminatory, somehow, to fat mare

indicators.note: somehow means the letters are put together in some unstated way

explanation.surface: A fat mare's sense of taste is discerning.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in: put the answer before 'taste' to get a phrase meaning a question of personal judgement. The anagram signal is the word after 'discriminatory', acting on TO FAT MARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a matter of taste depends on individual discrimination, so the phrase completes the clue's sentence.
